Class MKTooltip

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.MKTooltip
public final class MKTooltip extends Object
The single library entry point for queuing a hover-float tooltip, the one place a Component tooltip becomes pixels on screen. Every element tooltip and the panel-level tooltip route through queue(GuiGraphicsExtractor, Component, int, int) instead of calling vanilla's setTooltipForNextFrame directly.

Why this exists (the §0029 walk)

Hover tooltips had NO maximum width: a long tooltip drew as one unwrapped line stretching across the screen, annoying. The fix is a width cap, and the cap must be a library DEFAULT that every tooltip inherits automatically, never patched per element or per call site. The width decision is not element-specific (every tooltip should wrap the same way), and it is part of the emit call, not the per-widget trigger logic (which legitimately varies. Button suppresses on press, Dropdown gates trigger-vs-popover). The one substrate all ~16 tooltip sites already shared was the single vanilla call graphics.setTooltipForNextFrame(font, component, mx, my). So the missing primitive is a thin wrapper over exactly that call, this class.

The exception to adaptive-width-as-default

Pass 3 made adaptive (grow-to-content) width the default for laid-out panel content. A hover tooltip is the deliberate exception: it is a mouse-follower float with no containing layout to bound it, so "grow to content" is exactly what produces the across-the-screen line. Capping the tooltip is the tooltip-surface analogue of the screen-edge ceiling that already bounds panels same intent (don't let a float run to the screen edge), applied to the one surface the panel machinery doesn't reach. The cap reuses Font.split, the same vanilla wrapper TextLabel's adaptive path uses, so the two layers share a wrapping vocabulary without sharing code.

    • DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH

      public static final int DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH
      Library-default maximum hover-tooltip width, in GUI pixels. Sized to about seven average words: ~7 words averaging ~5 chars + a space ≈ 40 chars, and Minecraft's default font averages ~6px per glyph (incl. the 1px gap), so ≈ 200px. A tooltip wider than this wraps onto multiple lines rather than drawing as one long horizontal line. Tunable, the sane band is roughly 180 to 220; widen if seven words feels too tight in-game.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Method Details

    • hideWhen

      public static void hideWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Hides every tooltip in the game, on any screen and from any source (vanilla, MenuKit elements, other mods), on every frame condition is true. Several mods may register; any one returning true hides. Registering the same supplier instance twice is a no-op. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • hidden

      @Internal public static boolean hidden()
      True when any registered hideWhen(BooleanSupplier) predicate holds this frame.

    • wrapWhen

      public static void wrapWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Wraps every tooltip to the screen's width on every frame condition is true: a text line wider than wrapWidth(int) breaks onto more lines (vanilla's splitter, breaking at spaces) and the tooltip is kept inside the screen's sides. Images (a bundle's grid, a map) are left as they are. A wrapped first line stays one title: the gap under it and the scroll pin take all of its lines. Several mods may register; any one returning true wraps. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • clampWhen

      public static void clampWhen(BooleanSupplier condition)
      Keeps every tooltip's top at least EDGE below the top of the screen on every frame condition is true. A tooltip taller than the screen then starts at the top, title first, and runs off the bottom; scrollBy(int, int) with a negative y brings up the rest, as far as its last line. Several mods may register; any one returning true clamps. Call from client init.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze

    • fitX

      @Internal public static int fitX(int x, int width, int screenWidth)
      Where a tooltip's text starts so its background stays EDGE inside both sides of the screen. Vanilla flips a wide tooltip to the cursor's left but lets one just under the screen's width hang off the right; this pulls it in. One wider than wrapWidth(int) (an image) goes to the left edge, as vanilla puts it.

    • wrapped

      @Internal public static List<net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.tooltip.ClientTooltipComponent> wrapped(net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, List<net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.tooltip.ClientTooltipComponent> lines, int screenWidth)
      lines with every text line wider than wrapWidth(int) split by vanilla's Font.split. A split line stays one component holding vanilla's text line per piece, so a wrapped title is still the first line. Returns lines itself when nothing is too wide.

    • scrollBy

      public static void scrollBy(int dx, int dy)
      Moves the tooltip on screen now by dx, dy GUI pixels (positive y moves it down, bringing lines above the screen into view). MenuKit keeps it inside its own extent: a tooltip that fits on screen does not move, and one taller or wider than the screen moves only until its far edge is in view. While a tooltip is scrolled vertically with its top above the screen, its first line (the title) stays pinned at the top edge and the rest scrolls under it. The offset resets by itself when the tooltip changes or goes away.

    • clampScroll

      @Internal public static int clampScroll(int origin, int size, int screen, int offset)
      One axis of a scroll. Vanilla put a tooltip of size at origin on a screen screen long; returns offset clamped so the tooltip moves at most until its far edge sits EDGE inside the screen, and back no further than until its near edge does (or vanilla's spot, if that is further). A tooltip that fits gets 0; one that runs off an end can only scroll toward the hidden part.

    • contentKey

      @Internal public static int contentKey(net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, List<net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.tooltip.ClientTooltipComponent> lines)
      A hash of what a tooltip says, line by line, so "the hovered stack changed" reads as "the text changed" for any tooltip, item or not. Text lines hash their characters; other lines (a bundle's item grid) their kind and size. ponytail: 32-bit hash; a collision between two consecutive tooltips would keep the old scroll for one hover. Compare the strings if that ever shows.

    • queue

      public static void queue(net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text, int mouseX, int mouseY, int maxWidthPx)
      Queues a hover tooltip with an explicit max width, the per-tooltip escape hatch from the default. Pass 0 (or any non-positive value) to disable wrapping entirely and restore the old single-line behavior.

      Wrapping uses Font.split (the same splitter as in-panel text), which breaks on spaces and only force-breaks within a single unbreakable word as a last resort, so a single ~40-char word can still exceed the budget on one line, exactly as vanilla behaves.

      Parameters:
      graphics - the active GuiGraphicsExtractor
      text - the tooltip text
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      maxWidthPx - the wrap budget in pixels, or <= 0 to not wrap
